title: Insurance duty (Queensland)
summary: Queensland charges duty on general insurance premiums under the Duties Act 2001 (Qld): 9% on general insurance. It is paid on top of GST, so households and businesses pay more for cover of their homes, cars and businesses.
direction_rationale: The Henry Review found specific taxes on insurance deter people from insuring and recommended abolishing them all (recommendation 79), so that insurance bears only GST like most services.

verified.notes: An existing setting: no commencement date is recorded. The rate is from the revenue office's page; the Act's name was not on that page.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 28 October 2026 (phase 4, second tranche, of the productivity framework pivot) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: A tax on insurance premiums on top of GST. It discourages people and businesses from insuring and leaves more risk unpooled; the Henry Review recommended abolishing all such taxes.

marks.reason: Raises the price of insurance relative to other services, so people under-insure (Henry Review).

assessment.confidence_note: The direction is well supported; no official estimate of the efficiency cost of insurance duty was found.
